candidate.title: eCLIP
candidate.scope: Single unbranched Illumina eCLIP schematic, from an RNA-protein complex through 254 nm UV crosslinking, lysis, RNase I fragmentation, immunoprecipitation, RNA 3′ adapter ligation, protein removal/RNA extraction and reverse transcription to cDNA. eCLIP is the single target (enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation); iCLIP, irCLIP and HITS-CLIP are listed only as similar methods. The far-left title icon is not an extra branch. Primary-paper details clarify the two adapter interfaces and eventual readout; unshown controls, post-RT adapter ligation, PCR and sequencing are not added as depicted operations.

operations.label: UV 254 nm crosslink / lyse and fragment
operations.description: UV stabilizes RNA-protein contacts by covalent crosslinking, and lysis releases the crosslinked material for RNA fragmentation. The source caption groups lysis and fragmentation; its explicitly named RNase I digestion is represented by the next local operation.
operations.mechanism: UV irradiation at the depicted 254 nm wavelength crosslinks RNA and protein; cell lysis is reported by the catalogue and primary paper.
operations.information_effect: The physical RNA-protein contact is retained through subsequent handling as a covalent association.

operations.label: RNase I digestion
operations.description: RNase I cleaves RNA in the crosslinked material into shorter fragments while leaving crosslinked RNA associated with protein for capture.
operations.mechanism: Limited RNase I digestion; the yellow icons represent the acting nuclease rather than an additional biological target or product.
operations.information_effect: The RNA sequence neighborhood retained with the crosslinked RBP becomes the recoverable binding-site substrate; whole-transcript continuity is not retained.

operations.label: Dephosphorylate and ligate 3′ adaptor
operations.description: Dephosphorylation prepares captured RNA for ligation, and a 3′ adapter is joined to the RNA while the RNA-protein complex remains on the capture support. The output differs by its processed RNA ends and attached red adapter segment.
operations.mechanism: The primary implementation reports phosphatase/end processing followed by RNA ligase-mediated addition of a barcoded RNA adapter to the RNA 3′ end. The free red dash is adapter reagent; it is not depicted as a phosphate or a negative-charge symbol.
operations.information_effect: The RNA insert acquires a library-preparation handle. In primary eCLIP this adapter also carries a sample index, whereas the molecule-disambiguating N5/N10 random-mer is added to cDNA later.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Recovered adapter-bearing RNA is copied into cDNA, the blue-line endpoint. The P5, P7 and Random oligo labels appear over the RT-region sketch. Primary evidence resolves the random-mer as part of a separate post-RT ssDNA adapter ligation rather than an identifier installed by reverse transcription.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated reverse transcription creates cDNA and often stops at the RBP-RNA crosslink site. The drawing does not specify primer sequence or chemically map each colored P5/P7 segment; the graph stops at the depicted cDNA boundary.
operations.information_effect: cDNA sequence reports recovered RNA identity and mapped positions. Crosslink-associated termination can supply nucleotide-level binding-site information, with no guarantee that every endpoint is a crosslink. In completed primary eCLIP libraries, read 1 begins with the RNA-adapter inline barcode and read 2 with the later DNA-adapter random-mer followed by RNA-derived sequence; the random-mer helps distinguish independent molecules from PCR duplicates. Recovery alone is not proof of functional binding or complete specificity, and the paper uses controls not drawn here.
